source.title: Mixture-of-Experts Can Surpass Dense LLMs Under Strictly Equal Resource
source.authors: Houyi Li; Ka-Man Lo; Shijie Xuyang; Zi-Qi Wang; Wen-Zheng Zheng; Hao-Chen Zhang; Zhao Li; Shuigeng Zhou; Xiangyu Zhang; Da-Xin Jiang

record.tranche_reason: The study varies training data and compute for MoE models and reports validation BPC, a different measurement setup from the original scaling-law studies. Its experiments bear on loss changes with training budget, but do not fit or test the claimed power-law form.
record.gate_note: The study reports validation-BPC results for data/compute sweeps. These bear on V1, but the reported sweeps do not establish power-law scaling. MoE activation-rate comparisons, architecture ablations, and downstream benchmark results do not test the listed versions. Scaling laws cited for choosing learning rates, batch sizes, and dense-model shapes are not the study's own test of those laws.
record.test_reason: The study is about MoE vs dense comparisons, but its own results bear on two versions in an MoE setting. Fixed-N sweeps show validation BPC falling with tokens (Table 9, Fig. 1a), which the authors call linear on log-log axes; this bears on V1. A fixed-N shape sweep (Table 8, Fig. 4) bears on V4. No power law is fitted and the token range is under one order of magnitude. Kaplan shapes and Li et al. hyperparameter laws are used as tools only.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Authors conclude that MoEs with optimized backbones and an activation rate near 20% outperform dense models at equal N, C and D, using data reuse to equalise D. They draw no conclusion about the scaling-law versions.
record.recipe_differences: This study compares MoE and dense architectures under matched resource constraints; it does not fit the original dense-model scaling-law recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports that activation rate changes performance and identifies an approximately 20% optimum for its tested model sizes; this is an architectural result, not a test of the listed compute-optimal parameter/token scaling trend.

fits_no_version.finding: Repeating data for about 2 epochs costs little BPC under a fixed token budget. Using more than 2 epochs degrades 7B MoE performance (Tables 14–17, Fig. 2b, Fig. 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss under data repetition degrades only mildly up to ~2 epochs and worsens beyond that (data-constrained scaling), in MoE LMs.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed N and C, BPC varies non-monotonically with MoE activation rate, with an optimum near 20% at 2B, 3B and 7B (Tables 10, 12).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The compute-optimal MoE sparsity (activation rate) is roughly independent of model size.

record.problems: The reported BPC data/compute sweep is at fixed parameter count and changes data and compute together; the study does not fit power laws or test several orders of magnitude. The authors also state that they did not train models larger than 7B.
record.rows_left_out: Other BPC values in Tables 10–17 and the figures concern activation-rate selection, dense-baseline comparisons, or data reuse, rather than an isolated test of power-law scaling with tokens or compute. Downstream benchmark rows are also omitted because they do not measure the versions' stated outcomes.

untested.parts: Parameter scaling and compute scaling at an optimal allocation; power-law fit; ranges of several orders of magnitude (token sweeps span under one decade).
No extrapolation from small runs is attempted.
No compute-optimal N/D allocation is measured; N is fixed by design.
Dense-model shape effects; separating ζ from µ (they vary jointly); longer training runs.
Repeated-data runs are reported, but no power-law form is fitted for them.
Downstream accuracy is compared across activation rates, not as a function of scale or loss.
No fitting choices or exponents are compared.

missing.what: MoE shape sweep at fixed N≈2.15B: loss 1.674–1.699 across ζ 14–176 and µ 12.8–62.4
Dense baselines: BPC falls with D at fixed N. 2B: 65B→114B tokens, 0.4921→0.4808. 3B: 62.6B→125B, 0.4833→0.4684. 7B: 68B→130B, 0.4736→0.4594.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's limits_scope label for V1 was wrong: narrow range and missing fits are untested parts, not qualifications. Rows are single points, so per-row states are judged against the first point of each fixed-ra series. The authors' 'linear' wording refers to the log-scaled axes of Fig. 1a. Table 8 runs are short (loss ~1.68, cross-entropy rather than BPC), and µ varies jointly with ζ, which confounds the V4 reading.

versions.untested_parts: The study varies data and compute jointly at fixed model size and activation rate; it does not independently test parameter scaling, fit power laws, or cover several orders of magnitude.

relationships.condition: 2.15B MoE models at fixed activation rate, tokens raised from 1.14e11 to up to 5.41e11 (data and compute rise together)
relationships.reason: BPC falls monotonically with D in every series (e.g. 0.5235→0.5048, R1–R4; 0.5013→0.4872, R10–R14). Authors describe this as linear on log axes. The range is narrow and no fit is made.
relationships.display_finding: Bits per character decreased in every series, including 0.5235 to 0.5048 and 0.5013 to 0.4872, with trends described as linear on logarithmic axes.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: 2.15B MoE models at fixed activation rate, tokens raised from 1.14e11 to up to 5.41e11 (data and compute rise together)
source_check.reason: Table 9 confirms the stated monotonic BPC reductions, including 0.5235→0.5048 and 0.5013→0.4872. Section 5.1 describes the fixed-activation-rate traces as linear in Figure 1a, whose axes are logarithmic. Support is confined to the tested range; no fitted exponent or several-orders-of-magnitude test is reported.

source_check.notes: The pack lists zero rows for checking; row references in verdict reasons were checked against Table 9 without adding unlisted rows. The V4 evidence concerns training loss, while V1 uses validation BPC.

statements.correction: Table 8: N=2.13–2.16B non-vocabulary parameters; active parameters=366–370M; ζ=14.33–175.55; µ co-varies; training loss=1.674–1.699. ICLR 2026 publication, controlled comparisons and downstream evaluations are reported. Public checkpoints are announced; code availability is not established.
statements.problem: The shape-sweep numbers are correct, but the supplied text reports public checkpoints rather than a code release. Table 8 reports training cross-entropy loss.
